title: Consolidate continuous-batch handoff, KV freshness hooks, and I/O dependency upgrade
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Reduce tail latency and intermittent correctness bugs caused by race conditions during continuous batch handoff and stale KV cache reads. This ticket consolidates a lightweight handoff coordinator, formalizes KV freshness hooks (lease + epoch checks), and upgrades low-level I/O libraries to remove a subtle blocking path that amplifies variance under load. Goal is measurable latency reduction at 99th percentile and elimination of KV stale-read incidents reported in the last two incidents.

Background: Over the last 6 months we've seen recurring 'stale-kv' incidents and sporadic CPU spikes during high-concurrency streaming workloads. Root cause analysis points to three coupled issues: (1) the batch handoff path allows in-flight sessions to read slightly stale KV entries during shard rebinds; (2) there is no explicit freshness hook between the scheduler lease renewals and KV epoch reconciliation; (3) an older async I/O dependency has a fallback that sometimes performs synchronous fsync-ish calls on error paths, exacerbating jitter.

Scope & deliverables:
- Introduce a lightweight HandOffCoordinator component that sequences batch ownership transitions with minimal serialization (cooperative handoff using epoch tokens).
- Add KV freshness hooks: lease_epoch and observe_epoch checks exposed on the public kvcache API; ensure read-path consults in-memory epoch before returning cached entries while allowing fast-path hits when epoch stable.
- Replace blocking fallback in io-layer by upgrading io-adapter dependency (libaio-wrapper -> io-future 1.4) and add a short-circuit path in the runtime to avoid threadpool stalls on I/O backpressure.
- Microbench harness and production canary config: end-to-end load tests (seq_len distributions), perf dashboards, and a gradual rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%).

Success criteria (must be met before broad rollout):
- 99th percentile token latency reduced by >= 12% on our simulated prompt mix (baseline: 280ms 99p for high-concurrency).
- No 'kv-stale' incidents triggered in 72h canary at 25% traffic; synthetic KV-consistency test (100k multi-turn sessions) passes.
- No end-to-end error increase > 0.2% and Pager SLI unaffected.

Rollout & mitigation plan:
- Feature-flagged merge, default-off. Canary in east-1 with traffic steering. Immediate rollback feature flag if error budget burn or elevated KV TTL errors. Add fast reconciliation job if we detect divergence.

Notes on alternatives considered:
- Full global lock during handoff (rejected: too high latency impact).
- Aggressive KV invalidation on scheduler events (rejected: too many cache misses, cost impact).

References and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/hand-off-coordinator-and-kv-freshness
- Perf dashboard (canary staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hand_off_kv/continuous-batch-cleanup
- Initial RCA: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1RCA-stale-kv-2026
